claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26, the Infrastructure Committee carried a motion reducing the time each approved public speaker could speak from the five minutes the Council Procedures Bylaw provides to a maximum of three minutes for that meeting, at a meeting for which about seventy people, between 60 and 80 entries on the committee's list, had been approved to speak on the bike-lane item.
claims.interpretation_notes: The primary count is 64 entries approved on item 7.6, within the specified 60–80 band. The committee's broader list covered other agenda items, and 52 entries are recorded as presenting on item 7.6. Using N-spoke instead of N changes the result to Partially supported under the primary band: the five-to-three-minute change is established, but 52 is below the band's lower bound. Under the alternative 50–90 band, N-spoke is within range and the result is Supported. N-all is 79 and remains Supported under both bands. The motion applied to each approved speaker at the meeting, not only speakers on item 7.6.

supporting_evidence.finding: Section 38(1) sets a maximum of five minutes for each approved speaker. Section 4 allows a Standing Committee to modify the bylaw by special resolution; section 2 defines that as at least two-thirds of all committee members voting in favour.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The standing speaking limit and the procedure and threshold for modifying it.
supporting_evidence.quote: Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.

supporting_evidence.finding: Under item 1.4, Councillor M. Janz moved to adjust section 38 for the 2026-08-26 meeting so each approved speaker could speak for a maximum of three minutes and each Council member had three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion. All six members voted in favour; it carried 6 to 0. The six votes meet the four-vote minimum required by the bylaw's two-thirds-of-all-members rule.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The carried three-minute limit, its coverage, mover, vote and result.
supporting_evidence.quote: each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes

supporting_evidence.finding: Item 2.3 lists five panels approved for item 7.6, with 15, 15, 15, 15 and 4 entries respectively: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 + 4 = 64 entries (reviewer's calculation). Fourteen entries carry organization names. The organizations are Edmonton Bike Coalition; YEG Bike Coalition; Bike Bus Alberta; Holyrood Voice; Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group; Paths for People; Ward Métis Bikes; Let's Bike There YEG; and Bike Edmonton.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The primary approved-speaker count is 64 entries, within the 60–80 band.

challenging_evidence.finding: The item 7.6 presentation lists contain 16, 16, 18 and 2 entries by panel, totaling 52 (reviewer's calculation). Twelve entries carry an organization name. This count is below the primary 60–80 band if the holder's queue figure is interpreted as people who actually presented rather than people approved to speak.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The recorded presentation count is 52 entries, below the primary magnitude band; it does not disprove the approved-list count of 64.

challenging_evidence.finding: Counting all approved entries across the four items gives 79: item 7.1 has 5, item 7.3 has 1, item 7.4 has 9 including the additional speaker, and item 7.6 has 64. This alternative remains within both magnitude bands but is not the primary item 7.6 count.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The alternative whole-meeting count is 79 entries; it does not alter the item 7.6 primary count.

limitations: The minutes page returned 403 Forbidden and the bylaw PDF returned 502 Bad Gateway when I tried to retrieve them. I relied on the complete carried text of the relevant minutes items and bylaw; the package states these are the same archived extracts supplied to every reviewer.
The meeting page's later correction or approval status for items 1.4, 2.3 and 7.6 could not be checked. The carried post-meeting minutes text does not report a correction to those items.
The agenda page also returned 403 Forbidden. Its carried item 7.6 extract lists five public-speaker attachments; the attachment titles are not reproduced here.
The item counts are entries, not distinct-person counts. The redacted carried text does not permit matching a person across the approved and presentation lists.

The minutes record no reason for the time-limit motion. I checked the carried minutes and agenda text and identified no City record stating a reason. No earlier meeting minutes were individually reviewed; web searches for earlier section 38 time-limit motions did not identify one, so no conclusion about how unusual this motion was is established.
unknowns: Whether any later approved minutes corrected items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6.
How many distinct people were approved, and which approved entries did not present.
Whether earlier Council or committee meetings since 2025-10-29 adjusted section 38 limits.
what_would_change_my_verdict: A corrected or approved version of the minutes showing a different disposition, scope or vote for the item 1.4 motion.
A corrected item 2.3 list showing fewer than 60 or more than 80 approved entries for item 7.6.
claims.suggested_one_line: The Infrastructure Committee carried a three-minute maximum for each approved speaker at its August 26, 2026 meeting; 64 entries were approved to speak on the bike-lane item, while 52 entries are recorded as presenting.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Yes. The committee voted 6–0 to reduce the maximum for each approved speaker from five minutes to three for that meeting. Its item 7.6 approved list had 64 entries across five panels, including 14 entries with organization names. The minutes record 52 presentation entries across four panels. These are entry counts, not distinct-person counts.
suggested_tldr: The standing limit was five minutes under section 38(1) of Bylaw 18155.
Under item 1.4, Councillor M. Janz moved the three-minute limit; all six committee members voted in favour.
The item 7.6 approved list had 64 entries (15, 15, 15, 15 and 4 by panel), within the 60–80 band.
The item 7.6 presentation lists had 52 entries (16, 16, 18 and 2 by panel). This is below the primary band if the queue is instead defined as those who presented.
The minutes give no speaker positions or reason for the motion.
calculations_needed: N-all by item: 7.1 = 5; 7.3 = 1; 7.4 = 9 (8 in the initial list plus one additional speaker); 7.6 = 64; total 79. Organization-bearing entries by item: 5, 1, 6 and 14 respectively; total 26.
The time-limit motion received 6 votes in favour from 6 committee members. Two-thirds of all 6 members is 4; the vote met the special-resolution threshold.

Primary band 60–80: N = Supported (64); N-all = Supported (79); N-spoke = Partially supported (52 is below the band). Alternative band 50–90: N = Supported (64); N-all = Supported (79); N-spoke = Supported (52).
